title: The zero-extension comparison
statement:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let $\psi$ be a
nontrivial additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ be a dense open immersion with finite
complement $S_0$, and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse
Weil sheaf on $U_0$ (irreducible among lisse Weil sheaves: its only lisse
Weil subsheaves are $0$ and $\mathcal M$) which is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] and punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Let $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ be a dense open immersion
into the dual line and $\mathcal M'$ a lisse Weil sheaf on $U'_0$ such
that $\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong
(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]$ for the integral-transform formula of [def-fd-transform], interpreted
in the adic coefficient convention of [def-fourier-set] (such
data exist by [prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension]), and put

$$
\mathcal B:=j_*\mathcal M/j_!\mathcal M ,
$$

with $j_*$ the middle extension of [def-wf-middle-extension]. Then there
are Weil sheaves $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal B'$ on the dual line $A'_0$
such that

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(j_!\mathcal M[1]\bigr)\cong\mathcal G[1],
\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal B)\cong\mathcal B'[1],
\qquad
0\longrightarrow\mathcal B'\longrightarrow\mathcal G\longrightarrow
j'_*\mathcal M'\longrightarrow0 .
$$

The correction $\mathcal B'$ is lisse on the entire dual line $A'_0$, and
it has weights at most $w$: for every closed point $y$ of $A'_0$ and
every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of the local Frobenius $F_y$ on
$\mathcal B'_{\bar y}$,

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_y^{\,w}.
$$

In particular the transform of $j_!\mathcal M[1]$ is a sheaf shifted by
one without assuming geometric irreducibility of $\mathcal M$ or
unramifiedness at infinity.

proof.text:
Coefficient convention and equivariance. Work in the common-stage $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ category: choose a finite coefficient field $E$ containing the character values and representatives of the finitely many objects, Weil maps and inverses used below. Enlarge $E$ for any further finite diagram. The scalar-extension and descent clause of [prop-functor-package] permits all the calculations at this stage and their passage to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The Weil lifts in [prop-weil-operations] make pullback, tensor, proper/compact-support direct image, their comparison maps, and ordinary cohomology Frobenius-equivariant. Thus every isomorphism below is an isomorphism of Weil objects; we do not replace a Weil sheaf on a finite field by the invariants of its Frobenius. In particular the constructibility of $Rj_*\mathcal M$ follows from the direct-image clause, and its degree-zero truncation $P:=j_*\mathcal M=\mathcal H^0(Rj_*\mathcal M)$ is an ordinary constructible Weil sheaf by [prop-constructible-truncations].
Here FT means the integral-transform formula of [def-fd-transform] formed with the adic operations of [def-fourier-set], with shift [1]. Its kernel is lisse rank one and finite Tor by [prop-kernel-lisse]. Thus the constructible-domain clauses of [prop-functor-package] apply successively to pullback, tensor with that kernel, and compact-support direct image. Each is an exact triangulated derived functor, so this composite preserves distinguished triangles and finite direct sums. This constructs the required adic functor directly; no identification with discrete E-module sheaves on the small étale site, and no application of the updated finite-ring well-definedness theorem at E, is made.

source.place: Coefficient and Weil conventions; adic interpretation in def-fourier-set and the constructible domains of prop-functor-package

proof.text:
The boundary object. Put $i:S_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ for the reduced closed complement, and apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] to the ordinary sheaf $P$. Since $j^*P=\mathcal M$, this is the triangle
$$j_!\mathcal M\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow i_*i^*P\longrightarrow j_!\mathcal M[1].$$
For degree-zero preservation, [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] gives exact $j_!$ and $i_*$ on modules over the completed coefficient sheaf, and [det-sf-open-closed-pullback-limits] gives exact $i^*$. The rational heart is the essential image of the integral heart under the t-exact localization in [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]; together with scalar-compatible truncations (Step 1), these same exact sheaf operations give $j_!=Rj_!$ and $i_*=Ri_*$ on our heart. All quasi-compactness hypotheses hold for the complement of finitely many points on the affine line. The long exact sequence supplied by clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] therefore gives a short exact sequence of these sheaves: its preceding and following cohomology terms vanish. Its cokernel is $\mathcal B=i_*i^*P$. Decompose the finite reduced scheme as $S_0=\coprod_s s$, with $s=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, and write $\mathcal E_s=i_s^*P$. Sheaf sections over a finite disjoint union are the product of the sections on the components, which in an additive category is the finite direct sum. Thus
$$\mathcal B=\bigoplus_s i_{s*}\mathcal E_s.$$
The geometric stalk of $\mathcal E_s$ at a chosen lift is $E_s=P_{\bar s}$, with local Frobenius $F_s$ and degree $d(s)=[\kappa(s):k_0]$. Keeping $\mathcal E_s$ as a Weil sheaf on $s$ retains all its conjugate geometric stalks and their cyclic transport.

source.place: Step 1: boundary sheaf and decomposition over closed points

proof.text:
Geometry at a boundary point. Set $A'_s=s\times_{k_0}A'_0$, with projections $q_s:A'_s\to s$ and $\pi_s:A'_s\to A'_0$, and let $i'_s=(i_s,\operatorname{id}):A'_s\hookrightarrow A_0\times A'_0$. The finite-field extension $\kappa(s)/k_0$ is separable by [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius], so its spectrum map is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. Base change preserves étaleness and finiteness by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Consequently $\pi_s$ is finite étale; its degree is $d(s)$, since $\kappa(s)[\xi]$ is free of that rank over $k_0[\xi]$. Put
$$\mathcal L_s=i_s'^*\mathcal K_\psi=f_s^*\mathcal L_\psi,\qquad f_s:A'_s\to A_0,\quad \xi\mapsto s\xi,$$
where $s$ in the formula is the residue of the affine coordinate in $\kappa(s)$. This follows from [def-fd-kernel]. By [prop-kernel-lisse] this is lisse of rank one. The geometric restriction of $\mathcal E_s$ is constant on each of the finitely many point components; hence its pullback is lisse. In the lisse-adic convention [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], pulling back each finite-level locally constant sheaf and tensoring its local constant modules shows that
$$\mathcal F_s:=q_s^*\mathcal E_s\otimes\mathcal L_s$$
is lisse, with finite-dimensional stalks. The rank-one kernel is locally free, so this tensor is also the derived tensor used in the transform.

source.place: Steps 2--3: the maps over s and the lisse kernel with coefficient module

proof.text:
Compute the punctual transform, with arbitrary residue degree. Closed immersions are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and $\pi_s$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Apply the proper base-change clause of [prop-functor-package] to the square formed by $p_1$, $i_s$, $i'_s$ and $q_s$, obtaining
$$p_1^*Ri_{s*}\mathcal E_s\simeq Ri'_{s*}q_s^*\mathcal E_s.$$
The projection-formula clause for $i'_s$ applies with the finite-Tor second factor $\mathcal K_\psi$ (as [prop-kernel-lisse] states), and gives
$$Ri'_{s*}q_s^*\mathcal E_s\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi\simeq Ri'_{s*}\mathcal F_s.$$
Finally the composition and proper-coincidence clauses give $Rp_{2!}Ri'_{s*}=R(p_2i'_s)_!=R\pi_{s!}=R\pi_{s*}$. Substitution in [def-fd-transform], with rank $r=1$, proves
$$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(i_{s*}\mathcal E_s)\simeq R\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s[1].$$
This calculates the closed-point formula directly; the origin-only formula is not used for a nonrational point.

source.place: Step 2: proper base change, projection formula, composition, and the shift [1]

proof.text:
Construct the correction. The finite étale pushforward theorem [lem-a1-finite-map-lisse] applies to $\pi_s$ and the lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal F_s$; it identifies $R\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s$ with the ordinary lisse sheaf $\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s$. Set
$$\mathcal B':=\bigoplus_{s\in S_0}\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s.$$
A finite sum of lisse sheaves is lisse: at each finite coefficient level take a common refinement of their finitely many local trivializations and add their constant modules. This remains true upon rationalization and finite coefficient extension. The exact adic Fourier functor constructed in Step 1 is additive; its finite direct-sum comparison applied to Step 2 and the calculation in Step 4 yields
$$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal B)\simeq\mathcal B'[1].$$
All schemes in the finite étale theorem are separated of finite type over $k_0$, and its derived and ordinary pushforwards have the same coefficient convention fixed in Step 1.

source.place: Steps 2--3: definition, transform and lissity of B-prime

proof.text:
Bound the boundary stalks. Purity gives $|\iota(\mu_x)|^2=q_x^w$, hence the inequality $|\iota(\mu_x)|^2\le q_x^w$, on $U_0$. Apply [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] with $X_0=A_0$ and $\beta=w$. Its hypotheses hold: $A_0$ is a smooth separated geometrically connected curve; $U_0$ is dense with finite complement; and the nonzero lisse sheaf $\mathcal M$ has positive rank. Therefore every eigenvalue $\mu$ of $F_s$ on $E_s$ satisfies
$$|\iota(\mu)|^2\le q_s^w=q^{w d(s)}.$$
Only this punctual inequality is used. The finite-filtration definition of mixedness in [def-weil-punctual-weights] is not identified with a bare eigenvalue bound.

Bound the coefficient module on $A'_s$. For a closed point $z$ of $A'_s$, let $n=[\kappa(z):k_0]$ and $r=n/d(s)$. The residue inclusion $\kappa(s)\hookrightarrow\kappa(z)$ gives this positive integer. The pullback Weil map on $q_s^*\mathcal E_s$ is the pullback of that on $\mathcal E_s$ by [prop-weil-operations]. In the iterated definition [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], the degree-$n$ return is thus $r$ degree-$d(s)$ returns. The rational local-power statement [lem-trf-rational-local-frobenius-powers], at a common finite coefficient field, identifies its operator up to conjugacy with $F_s^r$; its hypothesis on reductions is satisfied by a free lattice on the geometric point components. It does not require a Frobenius-stable lattice. If $
u$ is an eigenvalue of $F_s^r$, factor $T^r-
u=\prod_i(T-\mu_i)$ over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. If every $F_s-\mu_i$ were invertible, so would their product $F_s^r-
u$ be. Thus some $\mu_i$ is an eigenvalue of $F_s$ and $
u=\mu_i^r$. Step 6 gives
$$|\iota(
u)|^2\le q^{wn}.$$
This argument also covers a nondiagonalizable $F_s$.

source.place: Step 4, second paragraph: residue degrees and powers on the coefficient stalk

proof.text:
Bound the kernel twist for the arbitrary character in the hypothesis. Additivity of $\psi$ and characteristic $p$ give $\psi(a)^p=\psi(pa)=1$ for every $a\in k_0$. The multiplication and inverse isomorphisms of [prop-kernel-lisse] give
$$\mathcal K_\psi^{\otimes p}\cong\mathcal K_{\psi^p}=\mathcal K_1\cong\mathbf 1.$$
For the last identification, the same multiplication formula gives $\mathcal K_1\cong\mathcal K_\psi\otimes\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}$, and the inverse formula identifies the latter with the tensor unit. These are isomorphisms of the kernel sheaves over $k_0$, hence respect their Weil structures. Pull back along $i'_s$ to obtain $\mathcal L_s^{\otimes p}\cong\mathbf1$. If $\zeta$ is its rank-one local Frobenius eigenvalue at a closed point $z$ of degree $n$, tensor functoriality of the Weil map ([def-wf-tensor-product, prop-weil-operations]) gives $\zeta^p=1$. Thus $|\iota(\zeta)|=1$ by [lem-tw-root-of-unity-modulus]. Tensoring this rank-one operator with that of $q_s^*\mathcal E_s$ multiplies every eigenvalue in Step 7 by $\zeta$. Therefore every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $F_z$ on $(\mathcal F_s)_{\bar z}$ satisfies
$$|\iota(\lambda)|^2\le q^{wn}.$$
This uses no trace-character parametrization and applies to every nontrivial additive $\psi$ allowed in the statement.

source.place: Step 4: weight-zero kernel factor; finite tensor-order argument from the multiplication and inverse clauses of prop-kernel-lisse

proof.text:
Identify the finite-fibre return operators in the rational Weil category. Fix a closed point $y$ of $A'_0$ and an embedding of $\kappa(y)$ in $k$. The scheme $Z_0=A'_s\times_{A'_0}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is finite over $k_0$. Proper base change in [prop-functor-package] identifies the stalk of $R\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s$ at the chosen lift of $y$ with the cohomology of the corresponding geometric fibre. The finite scheme has cohomology only in degree zero by [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology]. Apply [lem-a1-finite-weil-sections-decomposition] to $Z_0$ with the restricted sheaf, and take the summand indexed by that embedding of $\kappa(y)$. Its evaluation isomorphism gives
$$ (\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s)_{\bar y}\simeq\bigoplus_{\bar z\mapsto\bar y}(\mathcal F_s)_{\bar z}.$$
The comparisons are Weil-equivariant by [prop-weil-operations]. Hence $F_y$ is the restriction of the degree-$d(y)$ iterate of global Frobenius on these sections. The cyclic permutation of $d(z)$ lifts in the finite-sections theorem, restricted to this fibre, has length $e=d(z)/d(y)$ under that iterate. Its displayed return identity $F^{d(z)}=F_z$ on the component at $\bar z$ gives exactly
$$F_y^e|_{(\mathcal F_s)_{\bar z}}=F_z.$$
This is an application of already stated proper base change and finite-scheme evaluation, rather than an unstated extension of the ordinary étale finite-stalk formula to adic coefficients.

source.place: Step 4, last two paragraphs: finite direct-image stalks and Frobenius cycles

proof.text:
Finish the weight estimate by components. Let $\alpha$ be an eigenvalue of $F_y$ on $(\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s)_{\bar y}$, and choose an eigenvector $v$ and a nonzero component $v_{\bar z}$. If the orbit of that component has length $e$, Step 9 identifies the component of $F_y^ev=\alpha^ev$ as $F_zv_{\bar z}=\alpha^ev_{\bar z}$. Thus $\alpha^e$ is an eigenvalue of $F_z$. Since $d(z)=e d(y)$, Step 8 gives
$$|\iota(\alpha)|^{2e}\le q^{w e d(y)},\qquad |\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_y^w.$$
On the finite sum $\mathcal B'$ its Frobenius preserves the summands indexed by $s$; projecting an eigenvector to a nonzero summand reduces to this calculation. This proves the asserted punctual upper bound at every $y$, without any semisimplicity assumption.

source.place: Step 4, final paragraph: eigenvector argument and the normalized bound

proof.text:
Transform the boundary triangle and take ordinary cohomology. Rotate the triangle of Step 2 to
$$\mathcal B\longrightarrow j_!\mathcal M[1]\longrightarrow P[1]\longrightarrow\mathcal B[1].$$
By the exact adic Fourier construction in Step 1, its Fourier transform is distinguished. The isomorphism in the hypothesis for the supplied partner $(j',\mathcal M')$, and Step 5, identify it with
$$\mathcal B'[1]\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]\longrightarrow\mathcal B'[2],\qquad K=\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!\mathcal M[1]).$$
Use the ordinary long exact cohomology sequence, clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], for the standard t-structure at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ supplied by [prop-constructible-truncations]. Thus the cohomological functor is being used on the actual common-stage category, not an unidentified category of discrete coefficient sheaves. Both outside terms are sheaves shifted by one, so $\mathcal H^a K=0$ for $a\ne-1$. The degree-$-1$ segment is
$$0=\mathcal H^{-2}((j'_*\mathcal M')[1])\longrightarrow\mathcal B'\longrightarrow\mathcal G\longrightarrow j'_*\mathcal M'\longrightarrow\mathcal H^0(\mathcal B'[1])=0,$$
where $\mathcal G=\mathcal H^{-1}K$. Shifting this triangle by $[-1]$, both outside terms lie in the standard heart. Clause (2) of the same heart lemma puts $K[-1]$ in that heart, where $H^0$ is the identity. Hence $K\simeq\mathcal G[1]$. Truncation and every arrow lift to Weil objects by [prop-weil-operations]. This gives the required ordinary short exact sequence and the other comparison isomorphism. No geometric irreducibility or condition at infinity was used.

source.place: Step 5: rotated transformed triangle, ordinary cohomology and G

proof_origin.place: Steps 1--5, expanded with six-functor, finite-scheme evaluation and local-Frobenius-power interfaces; the kernel weight-zero argument uses its finite tensor order

blueprint_update.statement:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let $\psi$ be a
nontrivial additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ be a dense open immersion with finite
complement $S_0$, and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse
Weil sheaf on $U_0$ (irreducible among lisse Weil sheaves: its only lisse
Weil subsheaves are $0$ and $\mathcal M$) which is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] and punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Let $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ be a dense open immersion
into the dual line and $\mathcal M'$ a lisse Weil sheaf on $U'_0$ such
that $\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong
(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]$ for the transform of [def-fd-transform] (such
data exist by [prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension]), and put

$$
\mathcal B:=j_*\mathcal M/j_!\mathcal M ,
$$

with $j_*$ the middle extension of [def-wf-middle-extension]. Then there
are Weil sheaves $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal B'$ on the dual line $A'_0$
such that

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(j_!\mathcal M[1]\bigr)\cong\mathcal G[1],
\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal B)\cong\mathcal B'[1],
\qquad
0\longrightarrow\mathcal B'\longrightarrow\mathcal G\longrightarrow
j'_*\mathcal M'\longrightarrow0 .
$$

The correction $\mathcal B'$ is lisse on the entire dual line $A'_0$, and
it has weights at most $w$: for every closed point $y$ of $A'_0$ and
every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of the local Frobenius $F_y$ on
$\mathcal B'_{\bar y}$,

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_y^{\,w}.
$$

In particular the transform of $j_!\mathcal M[1]$ is a sheaf shifted by
one without assuming geometric irreducibility of $\mathcal M$ or
unramifiedness at infinity.

proof.text:
*Step 1: the boundary sheaf.* The map $j_!\mathcal M\to j_*\mathcal M$ is
an isomorphism over $U_0$ and $j_!\mathcal M$ has zero stalks on $S_0$,
so it is injective and $\mathcal B$ vanishes on $U_0$. Hence
$\mathcal B$ is supported on the finite reduced closed subscheme $S_0$,
and

$$
\mathcal B\cong\bigoplus_{s\in S_0}i_{s*}E_s,
\qquad E_s:=(j_*\mathcal M)_{\bar s},
$$

where $i_s:s\hookrightarrow A_0$ is the inclusion of the closed point
$s$ and $E_s$ is the boundary stalk with its Frobenius $F_s$, a
finite-dimensional Weil module of the residue field $k(s)$ of degree
$d(s)$ over $k_0$.

*Step 2: the transform of a boundary point.* Fix $s\in S_0$ and a Weil
module $E$ of $k(s)$. Put $A'_s:=s\times_{k_0}A'_0=A'_0\otimes_{k_0}k(s)$,
let $i'_s:A'_s\hookrightarrow A_0\times A'_0$ be the base change of $i_s$
along the first projection $p_1$, let $\pi_s=p_2\circ i'_s:A'_s\to A'_0$
be the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}k(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$,
which is finite étale of degree $d(s)$, and let
$q_s:A'_s\to s$ be the projection. Pullback commutes with direct image
along the closed immersion $i_s$, so $p_1^*i_{s*}E\cong i'_{s*}q_s^*E$,
and the projection formula for the closed immersion $i'_s$ gives
$i'_{s*}q_s^*E\otimes\mathcal K_\psi\cong
i'_{s*}\bigl(q_s^*E\otimes i'^*_s\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)$ for the kernel
$\mathcal K_\psi$ of [def-fd-kernel]. The pairing restricted to
$A'_s$ is the linear function $f_s:\xi\mapsto s\xi$, so
$\mathcal L_s:=i'^*_s\mathcal K_\psi=f_s^*\mathcal L_\psi$ is the
Artin–Schreier sheaf of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] attached to
$s\xi$, a lisse sheaf of rank one. Since
$p_{2!}\,i'_{s*}=(p_2 i'_s)_!=\pi_{s!}=\pi_{s*}$, the last because
$\pi_s$ is finite, the definition [def-fd-transform] gives

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(i_{s*}E)\cong
\pi_{s*}\bigl(q_s^*E\otimes\mathcal L_s\bigr)[1].
$$

This is the computation of the second formula of [lem-fd-first-formula]
(the case $s=0$, $E=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$) at a general closed
point. As the transform is additive, Step 1 gives
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal B)\cong\mathcal B'[1]$ with

$$
\mathcal B':=\bigoplus_{s\in S_0}
\pi_{s*}\bigl(q_s^*E_s\otimes\mathcal L_s\bigr).
$$

*Step 3: $\mathcal B'$ is lisse.* Each $q_s^*E_s\otimes\mathcal L_s$ is
lisse on $A'_s$. After the base change to $k$, the finite étale map
$\pi_s$ becomes the projection
$A'\times\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(k(s),k)\to A'$ from a disjoint union
of $d(s)$ copies of $A'$, so the direct image becomes a direct sum of
$d(s)$ lisse sheaves on $A'$. Hence each summand, and $\mathcal B'$,
is lisse on the whole dual line.

*Step 4: the weights of $\mathcal B'$.* Since $\mathcal M$ is
punctually pure of weight $w$, it is punctually of weights at most $w$ in
the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights], and the boundary
semicontinuity [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] on the curve $A_0$ with
$\beta=w$ gives $|\iota(\mu)|^2\le q_s^{\,w}$ for every eigenvalue $\mu$
of $F_s$ on $E_s$.

Fix $s\in S_0$, put $\mathcal F_s:=q_s^*E_s\otimes\mathcal L_s$, and let
$z$ be a closed point of $A'_s$ of degree $n$ over $k_0$. Its image in
$s$ gives $d(s)\mid n$, and the local Frobenius $F_z$ acts on the stalk
of $q_s^*E_s$ as $F_s^{\,n/d(s)}$, whose eigenvalues are the
$(n/d(s))$-th powers of those of $F_s$ and so have squared modulus at
most $q_s^{\,wn/d(s)}=q^{wn}$. On the rank-one stalk of
$\mathcal L_s=f_s^*\mathcal L_\psi$ the operator $F_z$ acts as
$F_u^{\,n/d(u)}$, where $u=f_s(z)$ is the image closed point of the line;
by [lem-fd-as-trace] $F_u$ acts by the $p$-th root of unity
$\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/k_0}(u))$. Hence every
eigenvalue of $F_z$ on $(\mathcal F_s)_{\bar z}$ has squared
$\iota$-modulus at most $q^{wn}$.

Now let $y$ be a closed point of $A'_0$ with geometric point $\bar y$.
The stalk of the finite direct image is the sum over the geometric
points of $A'_s$ above $\bar y$,

$$
(\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s)_{\bar y}=\bigoplus_{\bar z\mapsto\bar y}
(\mathcal F_s)_{\bar z},
$$

and $F_y$ permutes these summands. Its orbits correspond to the closed
points $z$ of $A'_s$ above $y$; if the orbit of $\bar z$ has length $e$,
then $z$ has degree $n=e\,d(y)$ and $F_y^{\,e}$ maps the summand at
$\bar z$ to itself, acting there as $F_z$. Let $\alpha$ be an eigenvalue
of $F_y$ with eigenvector $v=(v_{\bar z})$, and choose $\bar z$ with
$v_{\bar z}\ne0$, of orbit length $e$. Since $F_y^{\,e}$ preserves each
summand of that orbit, comparing components of $F_y^{\,e}v=\alpha^ev$
gives $F_zv_{\bar z}=\alpha^ev_{\bar z}$. By the previous paragraph
$|\iota(\alpha)|^{2e}\le q^{we\,d(y)}$, that is
$|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_y^{\,w}$. An eigenvalue of $F_y$ on the finite
direct sum $\mathcal B'_{\bar y}$ is an eigenvalue on one of its
summands, which proves the weight bound.

*Step 5: concentration and the exact sequence.* The short exact sequence
$0\to j_!\mathcal M\to j_*\mathcal M\to\mathcal B\to0$ of Step 1 gives a
distinguished triangle
$j_!\mathcal M[1]\to(j_*\mathcal M)[1]\to\mathcal B[1]\to$. The transform
is an exact triangulated functor by [thm-fd-transform-well-defined];
by [prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension] and Step 2, and after rotation,
this gives a distinguished triangle

$$
\mathcal B'[1]\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]
\longrightarrow\mathcal B'[2],
\qquad K:=\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(j_!\mathcal M[1]\bigr).
$$

Both outer terms have a single cohomology sheaf, in degree $-1$. The
long exact sequence of cohomology sheaves therefore gives
$\mathcal H^aK=0$ for $a\ne-1$, so $K\cong\mathcal G[1]$ with
$\mathcal G:=\mathcal H^{-1}K$, and in degree $-1$ it reads

$$
0=\mathcal H^{-2}\bigl((j'_*\mathcal M')[1]\bigr)\to\mathcal B'\to
\mathcal G\to j'_*\mathcal M'\to\mathcal H^{0}\bigl(\mathcal B'[1]\bigr)=0,
$$

which is the asserted exact sequence. All objects and maps carry the Weil
structure, since the transform and the triangles are formed in the Weil
category.
